transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I can’t seem to keep my head on one thing anymore. Like at work, I’ll be doing inventory, counting supplies and stuff, and then I’m just standing there wondering what I was doing. Or I go to the supply closet and forget what I went in for.

And I’ve been trying to study for this supervisor certification—well, I keep telling myself I should, because it would be a better position, you know, less running around with the mop bucket—but I’ll read the same line over and over and it just doesn’t stick. It’s frustrating. I feel like my brain just won’t stay on task.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I guess “down” is the word. Most days it’s like this heavy, flat feeling is just kind of there, following me around. Like even if I’m just pushing the cleaning cart down one of those empty hallways at work, it’s there.

And then I’ll be at home with my family, trying to act normal, you know, like listening and nodding, and I still feel… not really there. It’s not always dramatic or anything, just this dull weight that doesn’t really leave.
Have you noticed any worsening in your memory or thinking lately, like forgetting things more often than before or having trouble with tasks that used to be easy for you?

Yeah, that’s actually the main reason I came in. My head just doesn’t stay on task like it used to. I’ll be doing inventory at work, counting bottles or paper towels or whatever, and then I lose the thread and have to start over.

Or I’ll walk to the supply closet and just stand there like, why did I come in here? Which is embarrassing, especially if somebody else is waiting on something. And with the supervisor certification, I’ll sit down to study, and I keep reading the same line over and over, like it’s not going in. It makes me feel kind of stuck.
Do you feel that your trouble with memory and concentration started after you began feeling this heavy, low mood, or were you having these problems before your mood changed?

I think the concentration stuff is kind of what made me notice everything, honestly. Like, I came in because my head just doesn’t stay on one thing anymore. I’ll be doing inventory at work and lose track halfway through, or I’ll go to the supply closet and forget what I was there for.

The studying too — that supervisor certification thing — I’ll read the same line over and over and it’s like my brain just slides off it. I mean, the low mood’s been around too, but it’s hard to separate which came first. I just know the thinking part is what started really getting in my way.
Have you ever felt confused about where you are, or had trouble knowing what day it is, or recognizing people you know well?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like I don’t know where I am or who people are. I mean, I’ll lose track of stuff, like why I walked into a room, but I’m not looking around thinking I’m somewhere else.

Days can blur a little when the work schedule is the same over and over, you know? Like all the hallways look the same after a while, and Tuesdays don’t feel that different from Wednesdays. But I still know what day it is if I stop and think. And I recognize people fine.

Have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking that are getting worse over time, like forgetting things you used to remember easily or having trouble following conversations or instructions?

Yeah, that’s the part that’s been bothering me. I don’t know if I’d say I can’t follow conversations exactly, but my head just doesn’t stay on task the way it used to.

Like at work, I’ll be doing inventory and I lose track in the middle of counting, and then I get irritated because I have to start over. Or I’ll go to the supply closet and once I’m there, I’m just standing there trying to remember what I came for. It’s stupid little stuff, but it adds up.

And with the supervisor certification, I’ll sit down to study and keep reading the same line over and over, like it just won’t stick. Then I start thinking about how if I can’t even get through the reading, how am I supposed to move up, and… yeah. It makes me feel like my brain just keeps slipping off the thing I’m trying to do.
Have you noticed that these memory and concentration problems only really happen when you’re feeling down, or do they also happen when your mood is better?

It’s… not only when I’m feeling really down, I don’t think. Like even on a day where I’m not as heavy or I’m just kind of getting through okay, my head still won’t stay on task.

That’s kind of why I came in — I’ll be doing inventory and lose my count, or go to the supply closet and then just blank on what I went there for. And with the supervisor certification stuff, even if I sit down thinking, okay, today I’m going to be productive, I end up reading the same line over and over. Then I get frustrated and that probably pulls my mood down more, but the concentration thing is there either way.
Have you noticed that your memory or ability to concentrate is significantly worse compared to how it was a year ago, like struggling with things you used to handle easily?

Yeah… I mean, it feels worse than it used to. I don’t know if I could measure it exactly against a year ago, but I didn’t used to get tripped up this much by basic stuff.

Like inventory — I’ll be counting and then my mind just slides off it, and I have to start over. Or I’ll go to the supply closet, and once I’m there I’m thinking, “What did I even come in here for?” And the supervisor certification thing… I sit there reading the same line over and over, and it’s like it won’t go in.

It’s frustrating, because that’s partly why I came in. My head just doesn’t stay on task anymore, even with stuff I feel like I should be able to handle.
Have you noticed that your ability to focus or pay attention changes during the day, like having periods where it’s much harder to concentrate even compared to other times?

Yeah, I mean… I don’t know if it has a pattern by time of day exactly. It’s more like my head just won’t stay where I put it.

Like I’ll be doing inventory and I’m counting, and then I’m suddenly thinking about some other thing, and I’ve lost where I was. Or I walk to the supply closet and just stand there like, “Okay, what was I getting?” Which is embarrassing, even if nobody sees it.

And studying for that supervisor certification is the same thing. I’ll read the same line three, four times, and it still doesn’t really land. Sometimes it probably feels worse when I’m already tired or annoyed, but I can’t say it’s like, “Oh, only at 2 p.m.” or something. It just keeps happening.

Can you think of a time in the past when you were able to focus and remember things much better than you can now, like a specific task or responsibility that you handled easily before but would struggle with today?

Yeah… inventory comes to mind. I mean, I used to be able to keep track of that pretty easily — count what we had, what needed restocking, that kind of thing. It wasn’t exactly fun, but it was routine.

Now I’ll be halfway through counting supplies and my brain just kind of wanders off, and then I don’t trust the number anymore, so I start over. Or I’ll walk to the supply closet for something specific and by the time I get there I’m just standing there trying to remember what it was.

And the supervisor certification studying too… I know that’s not exactly the same as work inventory, but I used to be able to sit with material and get through it. Now I read the same line over and over and it’s like it just won’t stick. That’s really why I came in, honestly — my head just doesn’t stay on task like it used to.
Have you ever experienced episodes where you felt suddenly confused or disoriented, like your thoughts were really jumbled or you couldn’t make sense of what was going on around you?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not like suddenly not knowing where I am or what’s going on around me.

I mean, I can get kind of turned around in my own head, if that makes sense, but not like the room doesn’t make sense or people are talking and I can’t understand them. It’s more… I don’t know, I’ll lose my train of thought, but I still know I’m at work or at home or whatever.

Like the building I clean has all these similar hallways, and sometimes I joke they all look the same, but that’s not really confusion like you’re saying. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had episodes like that.
Have you ever had times where you felt unusually drowsy, confused, or had trouble staying alert, like your mind wasn't quite clear or you were in a fog?

Yeah… foggy, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it confused exactly. It’s more tied up with my sleep, I think.

My sleep’s been messed up for a long time now. Like after an overnight shift, I’ll get home and I’m exhausted, but then I’m just lying there, tired but wired, staring at the ceiling. And then sometimes I do sleep for what should be enough hours, but I wake up feeling like… like I barely rested at all.

It’s annoying because I’ll think, okay, I slept, so why do I still feel like I’m dragging? And then I’m at work trying to get through the cleaning route, and— well, the lights in some of those hallways don’t help, they buzz and make everything feel kind of unreal sometimes. But yeah, mostly it’s that my mind doesn’t feel clear when I haven’t really rested, even if I technically slept.
Have you noticed that your thinking or memory problems are getting progressively worse over time, to the point where you're having trouble doing things you used to manage without help?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of why I came in. It feels like my head just doesn’t stay on task anymore.

Like with inventory, I used to just do it — count supplies, remember what I needed, keep it moving. Now I’ll go to the supply closet for something and get there and just… blank. And then I feel stupid standing there, like I know I came for a reason.

And studying for the supervisor certification has been the same kind of thing. I’ll read the same line over and over, and it’s like it doesn’t go in. I don’t know if I’d say I need someone helping me do everything, but things that used to be manageable feel way harder now.
Can you think of times when your memory or concentration problems happened even when your mood was relatively okay, or do they seem to only show up when you're feeling down or flat?

I think it’s worse when I’m feeling really flat, yeah… like everything takes more effort then. But honestly, it’s hard for me to separate it out cleanly.

The main thing is just my head doesn’t stay on task anymore. Like I’ll be doing inventory and go to the supply closet, and by the time I get there I’m standing there thinking, what was I even getting? And with the supervisor certification stuff, I’ll read the same line over and over and it just doesn’t stick.

Sometimes I’ll be in an okay mood, or at least not feeling especially bad, and it still happens. But then I start getting frustrated about it, and that kind of drags my mood down too, so… it all sort of runs together.

Have you noticed any physical changes or medical conditions recently that might explain these problems with your memory and concentration, like a head injury, stroke, or a condition affecting your brain?

I don’t think so… nothing that I can point to like that. I mean, I haven’t had anything where I’m like, “Oh yeah, that explains it.”

Sometimes I wonder if it’s just me getting run down, because the building I clean has these long stretches where you’re by yourself and you start thinking too much, and then by the time I get home I’m still thinking about stuff I forgot to finish. But as far as, like, some big physical thing or something with my brain… I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Can you think of a time when your memory and concentration were clearly better, even for a short while, such as a day or two where you felt more like your usual self in terms of thinking clearly?

I mean… not really in a clear way. I wish I could say, like, “Yeah, last Thursday I was sharp again,” but it’s more like I’ll have moments where I think I’m doing okay, and then something stupid happens and it reminds me.

Like at work, with inventory, I used to just handle it. Now I’ll walk to the supply closet and by the time I get there I’m just standing there, trying to remember what I even came for. Or with the supervisor certification stuff, I’ll sit down thinking, okay, I’m going to focus tonight, and then I’m reading the same line over and over like my brain won’t grab onto it.

I guess there are short stretches where it feels a little better, maybe if the day is quieter, but I don’t know that I’ve had a whole day or two where I felt like my usual self. It’s more like… my head just doesn’t stay on task the way it used to.
Can you recall if there were any periods in the past, when you were not feeling down or flat, where you still had trouble with your memory or concentration like you’re describing now?

Yeah… I’m trying to think. I don’t know if I can separate it that neatly, because even when I’m not feeling especially down, I still get this thing where my head won’t stay with what I’m doing.

Like, that’s part of why I came in, honestly. I’ll be doing inventory at work, and I go to the supply closet, and then I’m just standing there like… what did I come in here for? And with the supervisor certification stuff, I’ll be trying to study and I keep reading the same line over and over, like it just slides off.

So, yeah, I think it does happen even when I’m not feeling totally flat. But then I get annoyed at myself, and I start thinking about how I used to be able to handle this stuff better, and then my mood kind of follows it down. So it’s hard to say, “This was a clean period where my mood was fine but my focus wasn’t.” It all gets mixed together.
Can you think of a time when your mood was clearly better, like a day when you felt more like your usual self emotionally, but you still had trouble remembering things or staying focused?

Yeah… I think so, sort of. Like there are days where I’m not feeling as weighed down, maybe I’m joking a little at work or I get home and I’m not in that same hole, but my head still does that thing where it just won’t stay on task.

That’s really why I came in, because it’s messing with normal stuff. I’ll be doing inventory and go to the supply closet, and then I’m standing there thinking, “What was I here for?” And with the supervisor certification, even if I’m in a better mood, I’ll sit there reading the same line over and over, like it won’t stick.

I mean, sometimes I wonder if I’m just distracted because the building gets quiet and my mind wanders, but… yeah, even when I’m more like myself emotionally, the focus and remembering still isn’t right.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least a few days when your mood was clearly better and your memory and concentration also felt noticeably improved?

I don’t think I’ve had a few days where both things felt clearly better, no. I mean, maybe I’ll have a decent shift where I’m not as dragged down, and I’m talking with people a little more, but my head still… it still slips.

Like I came in because it’s been getting in the way. I’ll be doing inventory and walk to the supply closet, and then I’m just standing there trying to remember why I went in there. Or I’ll try to study for the supervisor certification, and I’m reading the same line again and again and it’s like nothing sticks.

So if there were little moments that were better, they didn’t last a few days, and they didn’t feel like I was really back to normal.

Can you recall any specific tasks or responsibilities at work or home from a few years ago that you handled easily, but now you would struggle to complete because of your memory or concentration problems?

Yeah… inventory is the first thing that comes to mind. A few years ago I could keep track of what supplies we had, what needed restocking, all that, without making such a production out of it. Now I’ll go to the supply closet and just kind of blank out, like, “Why did I come in here?”

And the supervisor certification studying, too. I mean, that’s not exactly home stuff, but it’s after work sometimes, and I used to be able to sit down and get through material. Now I keep reading the same line over and over and it just doesn’t stay in my head.

It’s frustrating because it’s not like these are complicated things all the time. It’s like my head just doesn’t stay on the task anymore.
